**Market Pulse:** S&P 500 closed at 7,625 (-0.5%), NASDAQ at 25,990 (-0.1%), and TSX Composite at 35,569 (-1.1%). Oil prices climbing added to producer inflation concerns and weighed on TSX futures. The Bank of Canada decision on October 28 and the Fed's next move remain the key macro anchors, with markets pricing limited cuts. About 15 days ago we picked AVGO on an AI-chip catalyst and it closed down 6.58 percent, a reminder that sector rotation can override single-name momentum even on positive news. Energy and materials led the downside while select consumer staples showed relative resilience. Canada's Raw Materials Price Index rose 4.8 percent month on month in September, led by a 14.4 percent climb in crude oil, while producer prices advanced 2.0 percent month on month. Mullen Group jumped 11.5 percent to $32.28 after reporting record third-quarter results with revenue up 16.3 percent year-over-year and net profit surging over 55 percent to $51.5 million. Waste Connections and FirstService each rose more than 7 percent on their own quarterly earnings that showed revenue growth and raised outlooks. TSX futures point to a cautious open today as hotter producer inflation data raises the prospect of borrowing costs staying higher for longer.

### Strategy Spotlight
Dividend-focused ETFs and split-share structures let investors collect income while the underlying holdings provide capital appreciation potential. Today's announcements of quarterly distributions from several Middlefield funds highlight how these vehicles deliver predictable cash flow on a set schedule. Middlefield Global Infrastructure Dividend ETF (TSX: MINF) will pay $0.04167 per unit with record date October 31, 2026 and payable date November 13, 2026. Investors can use the distribution reinvestment plan offered by these funds to compound holdings commission-free inside a TFSA or RRSP. The approach works best in sideways or modestly rising markets where the yield cushions volatility. Risks include NAV erosion if underlying holdings decline and tax treatment differences between registered and non-registered accounts. Compare the stated distribution amount against the fund's payout ratio and recent performance before allocating. Middlefield, founded in 1979, manages income-focused strategies across global fixed income and equities with offices in Toronto and London. Canadian investors can hold these units in registered accounts to defer or eliminate tax on the distributions until withdrawal. The same record and payable dates across the funds simplify cash-flow planning for those building laddered income portfolios. Source: [financialpost.com](https://financialpost.com/globe-newswire/middlefield-global-infrastructure-dividend-etf-distributions-6)
---
### Investor Education: Account Prioritization Mechanics
A Canadian investor with $10,000 available today must decide whether that cash enters the TFSA, RRSP, or FHSA first because each account carries different contribution-room rules and tax treatment on withdrawals. The TFSA grows tax-free with no tax on withdrawal, the RRSP delivers an immediate tax refund but taxes withdrawals as income, and the FHSA combines both benefits only for first-time home buyers. The correct order depends on current marginal tax rate, expected future tax rate, and whether home ownership is a near-term goal. Placing funds in the wrong account first can leave thousands in lost tax savings over a decade. The practical check is to model the after-tax outcome of each account choice using the investor's own tax bracket before transferring the cash. Contribution room in a TFSA carries forward indefinitely, while RRSP room resets each year based on earned income, and FHSA room is capped at a lifetime limit of $40,000. A higher current tax rate favors the RRSP for the immediate deduction, whereas a lower expected future rate favors the TFSA for tax-free growth. The Motley Fool Canada article outlines a simple priority sequence that begins with the FHSA if home purchase is planned within 15 years, followed by the TFSA for flexibility, then the RRSP for the tax refund. Dividend payers such as Scotiabank fit inside any of these accounts, but the tax credit on eligible Canadian dividends provides an extra advantage only in non-registered accounts. Modeling a $10,000 contribution at a 40 percent marginal rate shows an immediate $4,000 refund in the RRSP versus zero in the TFSA, yet the TFSA preserves full access without clawback on future income-tested benefits. The article notes that the TFSA offers the most flexibility for any future need while the RRSP provides the largest upfront tax saving when income is high. Investors should also consider that FHSA contributions can be transferred tax-free to an RRSP if home purchase plans change. The choice between accounts ultimately hinges on whether the investor values immediate tax relief, long-term tax-free growth, or the specific home-buying incentive. Running the numbers with current contribution room and projected tax brackets prevents costly sequencing errors that compound over decades. Source: [fool.ca](https://www.fool.ca/2026/10/23/which-account-should-you-fill-first-for-retirement/)

# Modern Investing Techniques
💰 **Modern Investing Techniques** — AI-Powered Daily Market Intelligence
> **CIBC shares sit roughly 7% below the CA$170.50 fair-value estimate after the bank priced $1 billion in long-dated notes.**

**Market Pulse:** The S&P 500 closed at 7,713 (+0.3%), the NASDAQ Composite at 26,425 (flat), and the TSX Composite at 36,108 (+0.5%). About 14 days ago we picked AMD on a catalyst play for potential Samsung partnership in semiconductors and it closed down 4.61%. A growing number of economists now see odds rising for a Bank of Canada rate hike next week as inflation stays stubborn. Financials led gains on the TSX while energy lagged despite oil moving higher. The nearest central-bank decisions remain the Bank of Canada on October 29 and the Fed later in the year, with markets pricing a hold from both. Canadian housing data shows the market on its knees with borrowing costs potentially rising if the central bank shifts from its July 2023 hold pattern. Enbridge pipeline volumes and dividend coverage remain key watch items for income portfolios as the company signals possible future payout growth.
---
### Strategy Spotlight
Thematic investing in Canadian AI names delivered outsized returns when investors focused on companies already posting revenue growth above 30% and trading at reasonable multiples to that growth. The approach works by screening for sector leadership in an emerging theme, then confirming the names have already beaten the TSX by wide margins before adding exposure. In today’s tape, two Canadian AI picks have locked in +78% and +71% gains while the broader index lagged, showing the edge comes from early identification of the theme rather than chasing after the move is obvious. Implementation starts with a simple screen on Investing.com Canada or your broker’s sector ETF list for “AI” or “software” holdings, then cross-checks year-to-date performance and revenue growth from the latest filings. The strategy has historically worked best in the first 18–24 months of a new technology cycle when earnings visibility is still expanding. Risks include rapid rotation out of the theme once growth rates peak or when broader market volatility rises. One practical step is to allocate no more than 5% of a TFSA to any single thematic name and rebalance quarterly using the same revenue-growth and relative-performance filters. The two standout Canadian AI holdings also showed strong volume confirmation on their initial breakout days, which helped filter out weaker names that later faded. Investors using Wealthsimple or Questrade can set up a custom watchlist that flags software and semiconductor names with 20-day average volume above their 50-day average before entering. Historical data from prior tech cycles shows that names beating the TSX by more than 50% in the first year of a theme often continue to outperform for another 12 months if revenue growth remains above 25%. The current setup benefits from sector rotation into technology as financials and energy lag, creating a window for disciplined thematic entries rather than broad index purchases. Source: [ca.investing.com](https://ca.investing.com/news/stock-market-news/78-71-locked-in-the-canadian-ai-picks-that-beat-the-tsx--and-whats-next-4892414)
---
### Investor Education: Options Basics for Income and Protection
Imagine you already own 100 shares of CIBC at the current price near $159 and want to generate extra cash without selling. You could sell a covered call at the $170 strike expiring in 30 days for a $1.80 premium. That premium is collected immediately and lowers your effective cost basis to $157.20, but it also caps upside if the shares rally above $170 by expiry. The mechanism works because the buyer of the call pays you for the right to buy your shares at the strike; if the stock stays below $170 you keep both the shares and the premium. A pro habit is to check the option chain’s open interest and bid-ask spread before placing the order—wide spreads on low-volume strikes can erase most of the income edge. The common misconception is that covered calls are “free money” with no downside; in reality they reduce but do not eliminate loss if the stock falls sharply, and they limit gains in strong rallies. The one-sentence fix is to size the position so the premium income offsets no more than 2–3% of potential downside before you would normally sell the shares anyway. Canadian investors can execute this strategy inside a TFSA or RRSP without triggering immediate tax consequences on the premium received. The delta of the $170 call is typically around 0.25, meaning the position behaves like 75 shares of long stock plus 25 shares of short stock for risk purposes. Time decay works in the seller’s favor, with roughly two-thirds of the premium eroding in the final two weeks if the stock remains range-bound. Protective puts function differently: buying a $150 put for $2.50 creates a collar when paired with a covered call, capping both downside below $147.50 and upside above $170. The key difference from naked options is that covered strategies require owning the underlying shares or cash to secure the put, which limits leverage and margin calls. Investors should compare the annualized yield from the covered-call premium against the stock’s dividend yield—in CIBC’s case the 2.5% dividend can be supplemented by 4–6% annualized call income depending on volatility levels. This approach suits intermediate investors who already hold bank names for long-term dividend growth and want to monetize time decay without increasing directional risk.

A covered-call ETF strategy lets investors collect premium income on holdings they already own while capping upside in volatile markets. One way to implement it is to buy a broad Canadian equity ETF inside a TFSA and sell monthly out-of-the-money calls against it, targeting 1 to 2 percent monthly premium. ### Investor Education: Technical Analysis Fundamentals for Modern Investors
Suppose you bought shares of a TSX energy name at the open on October 19 expecting a rebound after the inflation print; the stock instead fell through its 50-day moving average by midday and kept sliding. The 50-day and 200-day moving averages act as dynamic support and resistance levels that many algorithms and institutional desks watch, so a break often triggers further selling from systematic strategies. RSI on the 14-day setting below 30 would have flagged oversold conditions, yet volume above the 20-day average would have been needed to confirm any bounce attempt. A pro habit is to mark the prior day’s low as the first support level and set an alert there rather than guessing direction. The common misconception is treating a moving-average cross as a guaranteed reversal signal; the fix is to require volume confirmation and a second indicator such as RSI before acting on the cross. Moving averages smooth price action over a chosen period so the 50-day line reflects the average closing price of the prior 50 sessions while the 200-day line captures a longer-term trend. When price trades above both averages the security is considered in an uptrend, but a sustained break below the 50-day often signals momentum loss that can accelerate if volume rises. RSI measures the speed and change of price movements on a 0-to-100 scale, with readings below 30 indicating the asset may be oversold and due for a technical rebound provided volume supports the move. MACD tracks the relationship between two exponential moving averages and generates buy or sell signals when its lines cross, yet these signals gain reliability only when accompanied by rising volume that shows genuine participation rather than low-conviction noise. Chart patterns such as double bottoms or flags can provide statistical edges for entry timing when they form at known support levels, but they fail more often than not without confirming volume and a clear invalidation point below the pattern low. The practical edge comes from using these tools together to time entries and exits rather than to predict overall direction, which remains the domain of fundamental analysis.

Next, compare the stock's sector ETF performance over the prior five sessions; if the ETF is down more than 2% while the single name is flat or up, the rotation risk is elevated and position size should be cut by half. You bought Enbridge after its earnings beat and set a mental stop at 5% below the entry. The stock drifts lower on broader energy rotation and you hesitate because the drop feels temporary. # Modern Investing Techniques
💰 **Modern Investing Techniques** — AI-Powered Daily Market Intelligence
> **Mortgage rates hitting seven point four five percent means Canadian homebuyers and rate-sensitive stocks face renewed pressure this week.**

**Market Pulse:** The S&P 500 closed at seven thousand seven hundred four, flat on the day. The NASDAQ Composite sat at twenty-six thousand nine hundred thirty-nine, also flat, with a year-to-date gain of fifteen point nine four percent. The TSX Composite finished at thirty-five thousand seven hundred six, down zero point one percent. About twenty-nine days ago we picked PNG.V and it closed down five point five nine percent, reminding us that earnings surprises do not always overcome sector rotation. The ten-year Treasury yield touched five point two zero percent for the first time in nineteen years, pushing mortgage rates higher and pressuring rate-sensitive names. The Bank of Canada and the Federal Reserve both remain on hold, with markets pricing in limited near-term moves.
---
### Strategy Spotlight
Comparing a company directly to its closest rival on the same day earnings land reveals whether outperformance stems from company-specific execution or broader sector tailwinds. Costco reported another strong quarter while Walmart showed slowing revenue growth, highlighting how membership models and operational discipline can sustain momentum even when consumer spending faces inflation pressure. Investors can implement this by pulling both companies' latest quarterly filings into a spreadsheet, calculating year-over-year revenue and same-store sales growth side by side, then checking volume on the day of release against the twenty-day average. This approach worked well during the twenty twenty-two rate-hike cycle when retailers with sticky customer bases outperformed peers by an average of eight percent over the following month. The risk is that one-time items or accounting differences can distort the comparison, so always read the footnotes before sizing a position. Canadian investors can run the same screen inside a TFSA using Questrade or Interactive Brokers data exports. The key is to treat the comparison as a filter rather than a guarantee, entering only when the stronger name also shows volume confirmation above its twenty-day average. Source: [fool.com](https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/09/25/costco-just-showed-why-it-s-a-better-buy-than-walmart/?source=iedfolrf0000001)
---
### Investor Education: Risk Management Position Sizing and Stop Losses
Imagine you bought Agnico Eagle Mines last week after its eighteen percent year-to-date gain caught your eye on a gold price dip. Your order filled at the open, but the position size you chose determines whether a five percent drawdown feels like a routine fluctuation or a portfolio emergency. Position sizing starts with a simple rule: never risk more than two percent of total portfolio capital on any single name, which for a one hundred thousand dollar account means a maximum two thousand dollar loss before you exit. Stop losses can be fixed at a price level, trailing at a set percentage behind the high, or mental when you commit to reviewing the position at a predetermined trigger such as a moving-average breach. The Kelly Criterion offers a mathematical way to size positions based on win probability and payoff ratio, though most retail investors simplify it to half-Kelly to avoid overexposure during losing streaks. Correlation matters because two precious-metals names can move together, turning two separate two-percent risks into a single four-percent portfolio hit. Drawdowns test psychology more than math, and the habit of cutting at the invalidation level rather than hoping for a rebound is what separates consistent operators from those who freeze. The concrete misconception to avoid is treating every dip as temporary without first defining the exact price or data point that would prove the original thesis wrong.
---
### Practice Investment of the Day
**Disclaimer:** This is a SIMULATED trade for educational purposes only. No real money is involved. This is NOT financial advice.

**Trade Type:** Weekly Hold
**Structure:** Shares
**Today's Pick:** AEM.TO — Agnico Eagle Mines
**Market:** TSX
**Sector:** precious_metals
**Strategy:** Valuation entry after gold-price choppiness left the shares at a reasonable multiple relative to recent production trends.
**Strategy Family:** valuation
**Hold Period:** 5 sessions from entry
**Invalidation:** Gold prices close below the recent choppiness low that preceded the eighteen percent year-to-date gain.
**Lesson Tags:** valuation_discipline, risk_management
**AI Analysis:**
- **Catalyst:** Reasonable valuation after recent gold choppiness, per the Motley Fool Canada analysis.
- **Technical Setup:** Shares trading at a reasonable price after the recent gold choppiness, with no specific RSI or moving-average levels provided in the source.
- **Risk Assessment:** A further decline in gold prices could pressure the name; maximum acceptable loss is defined by the invalidation level.
- **Target:** Modest upside if gold stabilizes, in the range of plus three to plus seven percent over the five-session window.
- **Confidence Level:** Medium — the valuation setup is sound but lacks volume confirmation or sector-rotation tailwinds in the current data.
**Why This Teaches:** This trade demonstrates how to screen for names that have already absorbed sector pressure and now sit at depressed multiples, then pair that screen with an explicit invalidation level so the stop-loss decision is mechanical rather than emotional. The approach forces us to define the exact condition that would prove the thesis wrong before capital is committed. Source: [fool.ca](https://www.fool.ca/2026/09/24/agnico-eagle-mines-has-gained-18-this-year-can-the-stock-keep-going/)
---
### Portfolio Performance
Portfolio Performance (simulated, one thousand dollars per trade): sixty-one total trades, fifty-two percent win rate, cumulative profit of three hundred five dollars and seventy-eight cents. The matched-window alpha versus the NASDAQ Composite stands at negative eight point zero four percent across ten rules-based trades. Average return per trade is zero point five zero percent, with the best trade returning twenty point one one percent and the worst returning negative eleven point eight zero percent. The current streak is one win, and the record began on August eighteenth, twenty twenty-six under the published rules of five-session holds entered at the next open.
---
### Tools & Techniques
**Interactive Brokers Option Chains**
Interactive Brokers provides real-time options chains with live bid-ask spreads and implied-volatility data that retail investors can export directly into a spreadsheet for covered-call or cash-secured-put analysis. The platform's API lets users pull strike prices, premiums, and expiry dates without manual copying, which speeds up the process of comparing income strategies across multiple names. Canadian investors benefit because the same account can hold both TSX and U.S. options, reducing currency-conversion friction inside a TFSA. Access requires an Interactive Brokers account with options trading approval; the data is included in the standard commission structure. Source: [bnnbloomberg.ca](https://www.bnnbloomberg.ca/markets/2026/09/24/sptsx-composite-down-despite-energy-sector-gains-as-price-of-oil-climbs/)

**Wealthsimple Screener**
Wealthsimple's built-in screener allows users to filter TSX-listed names by revenue-growth thresholds and dividend-yield ranges in under two minutes. The tool surfaces candidates that meet basic valuation or momentum criteria, then links directly to order placement so the transition from idea to execution stays inside one platform. It is particularly useful for TFSA users who want to avoid over-concentration in a single sector before committing capital. No additional cost beyond the standard account fees. Source: [fool.ca](https://www.fool.ca/2026/09/24/buy-this-stock-forget-it-thank-yourself-in-10-years/)
---
### Quick Hits
**Ten-Year Yield at Five Point Two Zero Percent**
The ten-year Treasury note yield touched five point two zero percent for the first time in nineteen years, the highest level since two thousand seven. Rate-sensitive sectors including utilities and real-estate investment trusts are likely to face continued selling pressure. 
**Action:** Trim exposure to long-duration fixed-income ETFs if the yield closes above five point two five percent on the next session.

**AI Chatbot Accuracy at Forty-Three Percent**
A Saturn study found that popular AI chatbots from OpenAI, Anthropic, Microsoft, xAI, and Google delivered accurate responses only forty-three percent of the time on average when tested on finance questions. Investors relying on these tools for quick research should treat outputs as starting points rather than final answers. 
**Action:** Cross-check any AI-generated earnings or valuation summary against the original company filings before acting.

**Jeff Bezos Thirty-Billion-Dollar Blue Origin Commitment**
Jeff Bezos has now invested a total of thirty billion dollars into Blue Origin, underscoring continued capital allocation toward private space infrastructure. Public-market investors can watch for related supply-chain names in aerospace and advanced manufacturing that may see indirect demand. 
**Action:** Add a small allocation to an aerospace ETF only after confirming volume above the twenty-day average on any breakout.

**Listener Challenge**
Open your brokerage platform and pull up Agnico Eagle Mines. Set a price alert at the recent gold-price choppiness low mentioned in the source article. If the alert triggers, review the position sizing rule we discussed before deciding whether to add.

# Modern Investing Techniques
💰 **Modern Investing Techniques** — AI-Powered Daily Market Intelligence
> **Chip stocks breaking out while the broader market stalls signals a rotation Canadian investors can screen for today.**

**Market Pulse:** The S&P 500 closed at seven thousand seven hundred six, down zero point eight percent. The NASDAQ Composite finished at twenty six thousand nine hundred thirty six, down zero point seven percent. The TSX Composite ended at thirty five thousand seven hundred fifty one, also down zero point seven percent. The ten year Treasury yield rose to five point one one three percent, the highest since July two thousand seven. Technology and semiconductors led daily rotation even as major indices went nowhere. The ten year Treasury note yield rose zero point one four seven percentage points on Wednesday. This was the largest one day increase since April nine, two thousand twenty five. Fed governor Michael Barr said in his base case further policy adjustments are likely needed to ensure inflation comes down to target in a timely fashion. Rising inflation risks and receding labor market risks mean the Fed was out of position and made an adjustment in the right direction.
---
### Strategy Spotlight
Sector rotation analysis identifies when capital shifts from one group of stocks to another even if the overall market is flat. Today's chip adjacent names all breaking out on the same day the broader market went nowhere shows how this works in practice. Investors can implement it by running a daily rotation view in a screener that flags sectors with above average relative strength and volume. The approach has historically worked best during periods when macro data creates uncertainty but specific industries still show independent confirmation. Risks include false signals when volume lags or when a single headline reverses the flow. A concrete step is to load the five names mentioned in the rotation report into a watchlist and check their one month and six month trend indicators inside an AI connected workflow. Historical context shows that when five chip names confirm together the sector often leads for several sessions afterward. Always pair the rotation signal with a same day volume check above the twenty day average before sizing any position. The five names included Monolithic Power up eight point zero six percent along with Seagate Celestica Teradyne and Analog Devices. Technology and Semiconductors both led on the daily rotation view according to the signal stack. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/OptionsPlay/status/2102748571917254787)
---
### Investor Education: Reading Volume Confirmation in Real Time
Imagine you bought shares of a chip stock yesterday after seeing the breakout headline and your order filled at the ask. The bid ask spread on that name widened from two cents to fifteen cents in the first thirty minutes because volume stayed below the twenty day average. What most retail investors do not realize is that a breakout without that volume filter often reverses within two sessions as the lack of follow through lets sellers step back in. The pro tip is to open the volume column in your platform before you click buy and compare today's bar to the twenty day line. The concrete misconception to avoid is treating any price jump as confirmation when the real edge comes from requiring volume to exceed the average on the same day.
---

- **Technical Setup:** Monolithic Power up eight point zero six percent with Technology and Semiconductors leading daily rotation view
- **Risk Assessment:** Setup fails the active rule requiring volume above the twenty day average before entry on any catalyst driven name already in sector rotation
- **Confidence Level:** Low — single factor present without the required volume confirmation that has scored positively in five closed trades

**Why This Teaches:** The current record shows that catalyst driven entries without the volume filter have produced negative average alpha. Waiting for the filter to align keeps the approach disciplined while the playbook rebuilds after the recent drawdown. Listeners learn to treat the invalidation line as an observable checkpoint rather than a feeling.

Portfolio Performance (simulated, one thousand dollars per trade): sixty one total trades, fifty two percent win rate, cumulative profit of three hundred five dollars and seventy eight cents. The matched window alpha versus NASDAQ stands at negative eight point zero percent across ten rules based trades. The record began on August eighteenth twenty twenty six under the published rules. Average return per trade is zero point five zero percent with a best trade of twenty point one one percent and a worst trade of negative eleven point eight zero percent on a current streak of one win.

### Tools & Techniques
**OptionsPlay MCP Server**
The server connects OptionsPlay data directly into tools like ChatGPT and Claude so users can pull strategy selection, trade ideas, and technical indicators such as one month and six month trend inside an AI workflow. It gives investors an edge by letting them run screening and rotation checks without leaving their existing research interface. Individual investors who already use ChatGPT or Claude for idea generation should request early access at optionsplay.com/op-socials once the production release is announced. Tony has been using it himself for the last couple of months to help build the research he shares daily. It is one of the top priorities heading toward production in the coming weeks.

**Meta AI Keychain Device**
Meta unveiled a new AI keychain device powered by Muse that brings Tamagotchi style interaction back in a portable form. The hardware gives investors a direct window into Meta's consumer AI push and can be monitored through the company's earnings and product updates. Users interested in thematic exposure to AI hardware launches can add META to a watchlist and track Muse related announcements on the company's developer channels. Mark Zuckerberg and Meta Platforms are bringing back the Tamagotchi with this new device. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/StockMKTNewz/status/2102909975060185387)
---
### Quick Hits
**US Home Prices See Fastest Annual Gain**
August marked the strongest buyer's market on record with price growth slowing as buyers gained bargaining power amid elevated costs and economic uncertainty. 
**Action:** Trim real estate exposure if homebuilder earnings next week miss on volume. Source: [x.com](https://x.com/unusual_whales/status/2102985880659198275)

**Doctors and Pharmacists Dropping Health Insurance**

**Action:** Review healthcare sector holdings for margin pressure and consider rotating into names with pricing power.

**NYC Reaches One Hundred Thirty One Million Dollar Settlement with DoorDash**
The city called it the largest worker settlement in its history involving food delivery. 
**Action:** Avoid adding gig economy exposure until labor cost clarity improves.

**Indian Insurance and Bank Stocks Tumble on Fee Cap Proposal**
PB Fintech Ltd led a slide in shares of Indian insurance companies distributors and lenders on Thursday after the country’s insurance regulator proposed caps on commissions and tighter management expenses. 
**Action:** Monitor Indian financial exposure for regulatory risk and consider reducing positions if fee pressure widens. Source: [bloomberg.com](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-09-24/pb-fintech-leads-slump-in-india-insurance-stocks-on-fee-cap-plan)
